summary: Backend-only verification that Telegram was split into two independent bots: PONTO_BOT (attendance) and MANAGER_BOT (orders, invoices, reminders, /status). 10/10 pytest checks passed covering (a) .env keys, (b) source references, (c) runtime URL/token used by each helper, (d) scheduler token, (e) tech punch import.
critical_code_review_comments: service_orders.py: send_ponto_notification / send_telegram_notification are near-duplicate — could be one helper parameterised by token to reduce drift risk.
Import of send_ponto_notification is inside the punch handler (runtime import) — fine, but consider top-of-file import to fail fast on refactors.
Prior iteration_37 flagged duplicate scheduler startup logs; still applies (out of scope for this test but noted).
PONTO_BOT_TOKEN and MANAGER_BOT_TOKEN live in .env unencrypted — acceptable for dev but rotate before prod.
test_credentials: n/a — tests exercise helpers directly with mocked httpx
seed_data_creation: None. Runtime tests monkey-patch httpx.AsyncClient so no real Telegram traffic is generated.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bot separation verified. test_telegram_bot_separation.py contains 3 groups: TestEnvSeparation (.env keys, no legacy TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN), TestSourceReferences (helpers reference only their own token, tech_extras uses PONTO only, scheduler uses MANAGER only), TestRuntimeSeparation (httpx URL contains the correct token, no cross-leakage). Tests use dotenv to load /app/backend/.env before importing modules. Old TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN key is fully removed. Chat ID TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID=6792830766 is shared.
rca of the issue: No bugs found — feature working as designed.
